sentences.text: 1 3 With the consent of both the parties matter is heard finally.

4. This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 10.3.2022 passed by the 20th Addl.
Member, MACT, Indore (M.P.) in claim case No. 1500287/2015 for enhancement of the compensation amount.

5 The relevant and necessary fact of the case are that on 8.9.2013 at about 10 pm the appellant/injured was driving his own auto-rickshaw with due care at a normal speed, when he reached near Choithram Chouraha, at that time respondent no.1 driver of the offending vehicle Bolero bearing registration No. MP-09-G.E.-9817 was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, hit the appellant due to which appellant sustained injuries on various part of the body.
The respondent no. 2 is owner of the vehicle and vehicle was insured with respondent no.3 at the time of incident.
Respondents no. 1 and 2 remained exparte before the below tribunal.

Respondent No. 3 denied all averments made in the claim petition by submitting that at the time of incident driver was not having any valid and effective license and vehicle was given without any valid effective fitness, the terms and conditions of insurance policy was violated, therefore the appellant does not deserve for any claim amount.
6
The Claims Tribunal after scrutinizing the evidence available on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.70,745/- in favour of the appellant with interest @6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, appellant has preferred this miscellaneous appeal for enhancement of the compensation amount.
7 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is against the law and facts and documentary evidence available on record.
He submits that the below tribunal has not considered the fact that appellant sustained permanent disability.
No compensation under the head of enjoyment of life, pain and sufferings, deformity, future medical expenses and other non pecuniary heads has been granted.
Hence, he prays that the impugned award be modified and the compensation amount be enhanced by Rs.1,00,000/-.
8 Learned counsel for respondent No. 3 opposed the prayer by submitting that impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just and proper and does not deserve for any interference.
9 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

10 It is established from the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record that the accident took place by offending vehicle which was driven by respondent no.1 and at that time the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
There is no material on record to show that there was any breach of the insurance policy done by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
11 The moot question to be addressed in this appeal preferred by the appellant is, as to whether the tribunal was justified in awarding the compensation of Rs. 70,745/- to the appellant.

sentences.text:
The appellant (PW-1) deposed before the below tribunal that his monthly income is Rs. 15,000/-
but the below tribunal has considered his monthly income only Rs 3,500/-.
The appellant was unskilled labour, he was not doing job as driver at the time of incident, therefore, his monthly income should be considered Rs. 4,000/- per month.

In view of the age of injured, the below tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of 15.
13
So far as the percentage of disability is concerned, the appellant did not produce any disability certificate which has been issued by District Medical Board.
The appellant has submitted certificate Ex.P-2 which was issued by Dr. Kushbandi (PW-2).

But the same cannot be considered as certificate issued by District Medical Board, therefore, in absence of medical evidence, the below tribunal has rightly held that appellant sustained only 3% permanent disability.

The below tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head of future prospects, loss of income for period of two months,
pain and suffering and other heads.

Therefore, the appellant is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 29,255/-
more as compensation under the aforesaid heads.
14 Accordingly this appeal is partly allowed and the amount awarded to the appellant by the below tribunal is enhanced by a further sum of Rs.29,255/-.
The enhanced amount will bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the tribunal and will be governed by the same conditions as contained in the award of the tribunal.
No order as to costs.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Manohar Pagare vs Ashok on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21740404/
